claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element automotive alloy with principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios.
The starting catalyst has low platinum-group-metal content.
A controlled low loading of CeO2 nanoclusters is deposited onto the catalyst surface after synthesis.
Deposited CeO2 nanoclusters form a heterojunction with the alloy catalyst.
The metal–CeO2 heterojunction creates oxygen vacancies.
CeO2 nanoclusters provide dynamic oxygen storage and release at the metal–oxide interface.
Dynamic oxygen storage and release prevents excessive oxidation of active metal species during transient and low-temperature operation.
The CeO2 modification prevents sintering of active metal species during transient operation and thermal aging.
The CeO2 modification stabilizes active catalytic sites.
The CeO2-treated catalyst will have lower light-off temperature or higher pollutant conversion than the untreated catalyst under identical low-temperature and transient exhaust conditions.
The CeO2-treated catalyst will retain activity better than the untreated catalyst after identical thermal-aging or mileage-simulation conditions.
The intervention does not increase overall platinum-group-metal consumption.
The intervention does not alter the bulk composition of the existing alloy catalyst.
The optimal CeO2 loading and dispersion required to balance oxygen storage against active-site exposure may depend on operating conditions.
